cmd.root.short: Liora CLI — Development tool for Liora modules
cmd.root.long:
Liora CLI is the one development tool to create, maintain
and publish modules in the Liora ecosystem.

Full lifecycle: init → create → develop → debug → audit → pack → sign → publish.
cmd.root.example:
liora init
  liora create module
  liora connect
  liora pack blog-manager
  liora sign blog-manager
  liora publish blog-manager
  liora audit
flag.sync_remote: update the remote module metadata before unlinking
label.name: Name
cmd.init.long:
Initializes a new Liora project by downloading the release
archive of the template protorians/liorian-socle (ZIP) and installing
the dependencies.

The release channel (stable [default], alpha, beta, rc) and the package
manager are detected automatically (bun, pnpm, yarn, npm)
and offered to the user.

The .env is generated from the template .env-sample (application key, VAPID
pair, project name/slug); each remaining variable is offered with its
suggested value as a placeholder (Tab to fill, Esc to accept all remaining
suggestions). Pass --auto-env to skip every question (project name, package
manager and .env) and accept all suggested values.
init.flag.auto_env: auto-configure everything with default values: skip the project name, package manager and .env questions
init.prompt.name: Project name
init.error.not_dir: %s exists and is not a directory
init.error.exists.fix: Choose a different project name or move the existing directory.
init.prompt.existing: Destination %s already exists and is not empty — how do you want to proceed?
init.choice.clear: Clear the contents of the destination
init.error.remove: could not remove the existing directory
init.error.clear: could not clear the contents of the existing directory
init.error.pm_none: no package manager detected (bun, pnpm, yarn, npm)
init.error.pm_none.fix: Install bun, pnpm, yarn or npm and try again.
init.error.clone.fix: Check your connection. If GitHub rate-limits you, export GITHUB_TOKEN and retry.
init.error.env: could not generate the environment values: %s
init.prompt.env_auto: Auto-configure the .env with the suggested values?
cmd.create.long:
Creates a new module from the reference mockup adapted to its type, renamed with the
provided identity: manifest.json, DDD tree (application/, domain/,
infrastructure/, presentation/), package.json.

The interactive wizard builds the module identity in three steps. First the
session is mandatory: the organization behind `liora connect` owns the slug
that anchors the identity, and an organization without a slug is forced to
define one through the CLI. Then the module type is asked among the canonical
kinds — it decides the scaffolded mockup (each type owns a reference mockup
shaped for its injection surface, spec module-types §2: settings for
CONFIGURATION, routines.tsx for SERVICE, widgets for WIDGET, token palettes
for THEME, remote declaration for WEB_APP_REMOTE, full application for
WEB_APP_LOCAL, Tauri administration console for SYSTEM) and the canonical
prefix of the reverse domain. Finally the reverse domain is offered pre-filled
`<prefix(type)>.<organization-slug>.` — the developer only completes the
module identifier, and the whole identity is kept for the rest of the process
(contract docs/modules/module-manifest.md §6.2: exactly three labels, prefix
config, system, service, widget, theme, else `mod` for web applications). A
non-canonical domain (e.g. com.org.module) gets its prefix rewritten to the
effective type.

The kebab-case identifier is deduced from the last domain label
(mod.liorian.accounting -> accounting). The interactive creation then asks for
the application name and optional information: version (default 0.0.0), icon
(lucide-react component), page url (application types only) and description.
--publisher overrides the session slug for CI runs and scripted replays.

The module unique UUID token is generated automatically.

At creation, the manifest.json is checked: required modules (requirements)
must exist (library/modules/ or src/modules/), and dependencies are resolved
through the detected package manager (bun, pnpm, yarn, npm).

Usage: liora create module [name] [--domain mod.my-org.my-module] [--id hello-world]
create.error.too_many: too many arguments — use 'liora create module [name]'
create.error.no_domain: provide the module identity: --domain (canonical form mod.my-org.my-module), or --id with --publisher
create.error.id_conflict: the positional argument and the --id flag designate two different identifiers
create.prompt.domain: Module reverse domain — complete the identifier
create.flag.mockup: directory of the reference module to scaffold, renamed from its sample identifier (default: the embedded mockup adapted to the chosen type — mockups/<type>)
create.flag.page_mockup: page.tsx template to scaffold the module page from (default: embedded page mockup)
create.flag.name: application name
create.flag.icon: lucide-react component name for the icon (optional)
create.flag.url: page path inside src/app/<url> (default: the identifier)
create.flag.type: distribution type: CONFIGURATION, EXTERNAL_URL, WEB_APP_REMOTE, WEB_APP_CACHED, WEB_APP_LOCAL, REMOTE_FRONTEND, SYSTEM, SERVICE, WIDGET, THEME (default: WEB_APP_LOCAL)
create.flag.category: store category (ADMINISTRATION, COMMERCIAL, FINANCE, OPERATIONS, COMMUNICATION, DATA, AUTOMATION, SYSTEM; default: SYSTEM)
create.flag.skip_install: skip installing the module dependencies (LIORIAN_CLI_SKIP_INSTALL=1 equivalent)
create.warn.mockup_ignored: ignoring --mockup %s: not a scaffoldable module (missing manifest.json or index.tsx); using the embedded mockup
create.warn.page_mockup_ignored: ignoring --page-mockup %s: file not found; using the embedded page mockup
create.warn.pm_none: no package manager detected (bun, pnpm, yarn, npm); the manifest dependencies (dependencies and devDependencies) are not installed
create.error.requirements_missing: required modules not available (library/modules/ or src/modules/): %s
create.error.requirements_missing.fix: Create the required module(s) first with 'liora create module', or fix the requirements field of the manifest.json.
cmd.create_view.short: Create a new view for a module
cmd.create_view.long:
Creates a new presentation view inside an existing module at
library/modules/<module>/presentation/views/<view-name>.view.tsx from the
embedded hello-world view mockup, renamed with the given identifier
(component <ViewName>, displayed title and description).

The target module is resolved interactively (or passed as the first positional
argument) and the view identifier is validated as kebab-case.

Usage : liora create view <module> [name] [--name my-view] [--label "My View"]
create_view.error.name_conflict: the positional argument and the --name flag designate two different view identifiers
create_view.error.no_name: provide the view name via --name or from the interactive creation
create_view.prompt.name: View identifier (kebab-case)
create_view.prompt.label: View title
create_view.flag.mockup: reference view file to scaffold from (default: embedded view mockup)
create_view.flag.name: view identifier (kebab-case, e.g. user-profile)
create_view.flag.label: title displayed by the view (default: the identifier in Title Case)
create_view.warn.mockup_ignored: ignoring --mockup %s: file not found; using the embedded view mockup
cmd.connect.long:
Authenticates the developer with their liorian-connect account
(email + password, MFA supported) and stores the credentials securely
(system keychain).
connect.mfa.non_interactive: this run requires an interactive terminal for MFA verification
connect.mfa.error.fix: The code is incorrect or expired. Check your TOTP app / your recovery (backup) codes.
connect.error.network.fix: Check your internet connection and the availability of liorian-connect. Also check the API URL — the `api.baseUrl` of `liorian-auth` in `app.config.json`, or the `LIORIAN_AUTH_API` environment variable.
cmd.disconnect.long: Removes all stored credentials and disconnects the developer.
disconnect.none: You are not connected — nothing to do.
disconnect.confirm.title: Confirm the disconnection
cmd.auth.long:
Authenticates the developer using the OAuth2 authorization-code flow
with PKCE (RFC 7636): opens the browser on the liorian-auth authorization
endpoint, receives the redirect on a local loopback server, exchanges the code
for tokens, then stores the session securely (system keychain).

The OAuth endpoints come from the 'oauth' entry of 'liorian-auth' in
app.config.json (authorizationEndpoint, tokenEndpoint, revokeEndpoint,
clientId, scopes).

In non-interactive (CI) mode, provide the authorization code via the
LIORIAN_CLI_AUTH_CODE environment variable to skip the browser step.
cmd.artifact.short: Module development toolchain (build, dev-server, pack, socle link)
cmd.artifact.long:
The Liora module development cycle, native to the `liora` binary:

  liora artifact build            bundle + host document (.liorian/artifact/)
  liora artifact dev              dev-server + HMR (SSE) — --socle also starts the socle
  liora artifact pack             build + D6/D16 validation + .LiorArtifactPackage
  liora artifact typecheck        tsc --noEmit
  liora artifact test             the module test script
  liora artifact bind:socle       link the module into the socle (symlinks + HMR wiring)
  liora artifact unbind:socle     remove the link

The bundler is esbuild (Go API): no Node dependency is required. The module
is the one holding the current directory, else the one named by the arguments.
cmd.artifact_build.long:
Builds the standalone esbuild bundle and the host document of the module
into .liorian/artifact/ (D7). The manifest stays the canonical declaration —
manifest.entry, manifest.artifact.{bundle,document} — that the
artifact.config.json config only specializes (templateData).
cmd.artifact_dev.long:
Starts the dev-server of one or several modules: bundle watched by esbuild, static
serving of .liorian/artifact/ and the /-/events SSE stream that reloads iframes
after every rebuild. The scheme follows the bound socle (.liorian/dev.json) — an
HTTPS socle forces TLS onto the module (mixed content otherwise).

Several named modules (`liora artifact dev crm billing`) or --all: a single
server, a single port, each module served under its slug (`/<slug>/`) and reloaded
independently (tagged reload). The bound socle's .env.local is aligned on the batch
(URL, module list, multi mode). A busy port (EADDRINUSE) falls back to the next
port with an explicit message; --strict-port fails instead of falling back.

--socle <dir> also starts the socle (`<pm> run dev`): the whole loop (socle +
library + HMR dev-server) fits in a single terminal.
cmd.artifact_pack.long:
Builds the bundle then produces the module .LiorArtifactPackage archive
(.liorian/build/): manifest.json at the root, sources under src/**, compiled
payload under artifact/**. The D6 rules (blocking typecheck, userScope) and
D16 (no direct network access) are blocking, as is the asset policy:
executables (exe, sh, bash…) are refused, only declared code, config and
media files travel.
cmd.artifact_typecheck.long:
Runs the module TypeScript typecheck (the `typecheck` package.json script,
else tsc --noEmit) — rule 2 of §4.4, blocking at pack time.
cmd.artifact_test.long: Runs the module `test` script with the detected package manager.
cmd.artifact_bind_socle.short: Link the module into the socle (symlinks + HMR wiring)
cmd.artifact_bind_socle.long:
Materializes the module ↔ socle link: library
(<socle>/library/modules/<id>/<version>/ symlinked to the module),
NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_MODULES_URL + NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_MODULES in the socle .env.local,
and the .liorian/dev.json development link in the module. Idempotent.
cmd.artifact_unbind_socle.long:
Removes the link laid by bind:socle: the marked library entry, the socle
.env.local identifier and the development link. A neighbouring real
installation is never touched.
artifact.flag.https: serve the dev-server over TLS (default: follows the bound socle scheme)
artifact.flag.http: serve the dev-server without TLS (HTTP socle)
artifact.flag.strict_port: fail when the requested port is busy (default: fall back to the next port)
artifact.flag.socle: also start the socle (`<pm> run dev`) — the dev loop fits in a single terminal
artifact.flag.no_build: pack the existing artifact without rebuilding the bundle
artifact.flag.all: develop every workspace module (`modules/<id>`) inside the same dev-server
artifact.pack.sign_hint: Unsigned archive — `liora pack` or `liora sign` applies the developer signature.
artifact.test.no_script: no `test` script in the module package.json
artifact.error.module_absent: module %q has no directory to build
artifact.error.pm_missing: no package manager available (bun, pnpm, yarn or npm required)
artifact.error.socle_invalid: %s does not look like a Liora socle (library/, serve.mjs or a `socle` package.json expected)
artifact.socle.started: socle started (%s) via %s run dev — socle, library and dev-server live in this terminal
cmd.pack.long:
Builds a module and creates a compressed .LiorArtifactPackage archive
(moved to .liorian/build/).

The version can be given with an '@' separator (e.g. blog-manager@1.2.0),
with --version, or defaults to the manifest version. --out writes the
archive to a custom path.

Without an argument, a selector lets you choose the module.
cmd.sign.long:
Manages Ed25519 digital signatures for modules: generates keys,
signs the .LiorArtifactPackage archives and verifies signatures.

The signature covers the canonical publication payload (module identifier,
version, archive checksum, manifest checksum, entry, type) and is mandatory
for publication.

Subcommands:
  sign keygen                  Generate an Ed25519 key pair
  sign <module|archive>        Sign a module's .LiorArtifactPackage archive
  sign verify <module|archive> Verify a module's signature
  sign trust                   Export the public key to pin in the socle

Without arguments, shows the SHA-256 fingerprint of the public key.
cmd.sign.keygen.long:
Generates an Ed25519 key pair and stores it in the system keychain
(fallback: encrypted file ~/.liorian-cli/signing.enc).

If keys already exist, asks for confirmation before overwriting them
(silent regeneration in non-interactive mode).
cmd.sign.verify.long:
Verifies the validity of a module's .sig file against its
.LiorArtifactPackage archive, using the public key stored in the keychain.
cmd.sign.trust.short: Export the public key to pin in the socle trust store
cmd.sign.trust.long:
Exports the public signing key under the key identifier the store publishes
as 'signatureKeyId' (the SHA-256 fingerprint of the public key).

The socle re-verifies every relayed artifact locally against a trust store
pinned at build time (NEXT_PUBLIC_MODULE_TRUST_KEYS = {"<keyId>": "<PEM>"}).
This command emits that exact material, so the developer side and the usage
side cannot drift:

  liora sign trust                     export NEXT_PUBLIC_MODULE_TRUST_KEYS=…
  liora sign trust --format json       the bare {"<keyId>": "<PEM>"} object
  liora sign trust --format pem        the PEM public key alone
  liora sign trust --format keyid      the key identifier alone (fingerprint)
  liora sign trust --merge keys.json   add the key to an existing trust store

A socle left without a trust store stays usable but never verifies a relayed
artifact: the verdict degrades to 'unverifiable' and the channel is trusted.
sign.flag.trust_format: output format: env, json, pem, keyid
sign.flag.trust_merge: add the key to an existing trust store file and rewrite it
sign.trust.error.pem: exported key is not a SPKI PEM block (missing %q) — the socle trust store would ignore it
sign.trust.error.format: unknown trust export format %q (expected env, json, pem or keyid)
sign.trust.error.merge_parse: %s is not a trust store (expected a {"<keyId>": "<PEM>"} JSON object)
sign.error.no_key: no signing key found in the keychain
sign.error.keygen.fix: Run 'liora sign keygen' to generate a key pair.
sign.confirm.regenerate: Regenerate the key pair (overwrites the previous keys)
sign.confirm.overwrite: A .sig file already exists, overwrite it
sign.invalid.hint: → The archive may have been tampered with or the verification key is wrong.
sign.error.pack.fix: Run 'liora pack %s' to build the archive first.
sign.error.sign.fix: Run 'liora sign %s' to sign the archive.
cmd.publish.short: Publish a module to the store
cmd.publish.long:
Builds and publishes a module to the store via the liorian-connect API.

Checks authentication, validates the manifest, builds the .LiorArtifactPackage archive,
signs the canonical publication payload (mandatory) and sends the artefact
to the store.

Flags --file and --version support the release session flow:
  liora pack ./acme-crm --version 1.3.0 --out acme-crm.LiorArtifactPackage
  liora sign acme-crm.LiorArtifactPackage --key ~/.acme/ed25519
  liora publish mod.acme.crm --version 1.3.0 --file acme-crm.LiorArtifactPackage
publish.error.not_connected: you must be connected to publish a module
publish.info.connect: Not connected — authenticating with Liora Connect…
publish.error.audit.fix: Fix the errors and retry, or run 'liora audit %s'.
publish.error.fix: Check your connection and try again.
publish.error.no_route.fix: The Developer Store API is not exposed by the resolved base URL: point liorian-connect.api.baseUrl in app.config.json to liorian-api-connect, or set %s.
publish.error.bump.fix: After a manual version bump (manifest.json), retry or run 'liora pack %s'.
publish.warn.version_conflict: An identical version already exists on the store: %s
cmd.link.short: Link a local module to a remote module
cmd.link.long:
Links a module created in liorian-connect with the local module (via its token).

Checks authentication, lists the online modules, and associates
the chosen local module with the provided remote token.

In non-interactive (CI) mode, provide the local module and the remote
token as arguments: link <module> <token>.
cmd.unlink.short: Unlink a local module from liorian-connect
cmd.unlink.long:
Unlinks a local module from its counterpart in liorian-connect.
The manifest.json token is replaced with a new local UUID token.

--sync-remote first syncs the local metadata (name, type,
description) to the remote product via PUT /api/developer-store/modules/:id
(best-effort, requires being connected).
link.error.not_connected: you must be connected to link a module
link.error.non_interactive: non-interactive mode requires the local module and the remote token
link.error.no_modules.fix: Publish a module first with 'liora publish', or provide the token as an argument: 'liora link <module> <token>'.
link.error.no_token: provide the remote module token as an argument
link.error.remote.fix: The remote token is invalid or the module does not exist.
link.error.none_linked: no modules linked to a remote module found in library/modules
link.error.not_linked: module %q is not linked to a remote module
link.error.multi: multiple linked modules, provide the module name as an argument
link.warn.no_remote: no remote module associated, sync skipped
link.success.synced: ✓ Metadata synced to the remote module
link.unlinked: %s is no longer linked to a remote module.
cmd.debug.short: Debug a module or all modules
cmd.debug.long:
Runs the debug of one (or all) module(s) in library/modules/.

Validates the module, resolves a build command (package.json script,
bundler or TypeScript type-check) and streams its output in real time.
A `debug`/`dev` script is treated as a dev server: it is stopped after
its start window (--timeout) and reported as started.
Press Ctrl+C to cancel at any time.

Without an argument, all modules are debugged.
debug.npm_none: no package manager detected, validation only
debug.no_build_script: no build script (debug/dev/build), bundler (esbuild/tsup) or TypeScript type-check found — validation only
debug.step.resolve.none: no build script, bundler or type-check found
debug.step.build.started: dev script running — stopped after %s (server/watch mode)
debug.flag.timeout: execution window for a debug/dev script, or cap for a build (0 = auto)
cmd.test.short: Run the tests of a module or all modules
cmd.test.long:
Runs the tests of one (or all) module(s) in library/modules/.

Validates the module, resolves a test package with the package manager chosen
at install (bun/pnpm/yarn/npm), installs it within that manager's scope when
needed and streams the suite output in real time. The chosen test package is
persisted in liorian.config.json. The run exits non-zero when any module's
tests fail.
Press Ctrl+C to cancel at any time.

Without an argument, all modules are tested.
test.npm_none: no package manager detected, validation only
test.no_test_script: no test script, runner (vitest/jest) or test files found — validation only
test.step.resolve.none: no test script, runner (vitest/jest) or test files found
test.step.no_tests.detail: no test file found — module skipped
test.no_tests: no test file found in the module — skipped
test.flag.timeout: hard cap for a test run (0 = auto)
test.flag.runner: test package used to run the suite (persisted in liorian.config.json)
cmd.audit.long:
Audits the conformance of one (or all) module(s) against the
Liora rules: Clean Architecture, manifest.json and index.tsx.

Without an argument, all modules in library/modules/ are audited.
audit.passed: ✓ Audit passed — no errors, no warnings
cmd.repair.long:
Automatically repairs the failing (blocking) points reported by
'liora audit' for one (or all) module(s): manifest metadata (id, name,
version, token, entry, permissions, platforms, compatibility, capabilities,
category, domain), the module directory name (proposed with a tab-to-fill
prompt, applied directly with --no-interaction), missing npm dependencies and
malformed manifest fields.

Findings that require a code change (Clean Architecture violations, missing
default export or module declaration, missing requirements, publisher
identity, empty assets) are reported as step-by-step instructions for the
developer to apply.

Without an argument, all modules in library/modules/ are repaired.
repair.flag.dry_run: show the fixes without writing them
repair.flag.no_install: do not run the package manager to install missing dependencies
repair.flag.no_interaction: ask no question (suggested directory names are applied automatically)
repair.actions.title: Automatic fixes
repair.instructions.title: Manual actions required
repair.nothing: ✓ Nothing to repair — module already conforms
repair.dry_run: dry run — no file was modified
repair.error.remaining: %d error(s) could not be repaired automatically
repair.error.remaining.fix: Apply the manual actions listed above, then re-run 'liora repair'.
repair.rename.detected: the module directory does not match the manifest domain
modules.error.cwd: unable to determine the current directory
modules.error.root.fix: Run 'liora init' to initialize a Liora project.
modules.error.module_absent.fix: Check the module name or run 'liora create module'.
modules.error.multiple: multiple modules available, provide the module name as an argument
cmd.marketplace.short: Search and install modules from the public catalog
cmd.marketplace.long:
Queries the public Liora module catalog (liorian-api-store)
and installs third-party modules into the current workspace.

Subcommands:
  marketplace search [query]   Browse the catalog
  marketplace install <module> Download, verify and install a module

The catalog API base URL comes from the 'api.baseUrl' of 'liorian-store'
in app.config.json, or the LIORIAN_STORE_API environment variable.
cmd.marketplace.search.long:
Browses the public module catalog: a full-text query, a store
category filter and pagination are supported.
cmd.marketplace.install.short: Install a module from the catalog
cmd.marketplace.install.long:
Resolves a module in the public catalog, downloads its .LiorArtifactPackage
archive, verifies its SHA-256 checksum and its Ed25519 publisher signature
(fail-closed), then extracts it into library/modules/.
cmd.dev.long:
Starts the application development server (project `dev` script)
through the package manager chosen at install.

The modules are checked first (debug + test): a module in error aborts
the command. Pre/post actions configured in the `toolchain` section of
liorian.config.json run before and after the command.
Arguments after -- are forwarded to the script.
Press Ctrl+C to stop the server.
cmd.build.short: Build the application for production (project `build` script)
cmd.build.long:
Builds the application for production (project `build` script)
through the package manager chosen at install.

The modules are checked first (debug + test + audit): a module in error
aborts the command. Pre/post actions configured in the `toolchain`
section of liorian.config.json run before and after the command.
Arguments after -- are forwarded to the script.
cmd.start.long:
Starts the built application (project `start` script) through the
package manager chosen at install.

The modules are checked first (debug + test + audit): a module in error
aborts the command. Pre/post actions configured in the `toolchain`
section of liorian.config.json run before and after the command.
Arguments after -- are forwarded to the script.
Press Ctrl+C to stop the server.
cmd.check.long:
Runs the project checks (project `lint` script) through the package
manager chosen at install.

Pre/post actions configured in the `toolchain` section of
liorian.config.json run before and after the command.
Arguments after -- are forwarded to the script.
toolchain.error.pm_none.fix: Install bun, pnpm, yarn or npm, or set project.packageManager in liorian.config.json.
toolchain.error.no_script.fix: Add the "%s" script to package.json, or map another script in toolchain.commands of liorian.config.json.
gate.failed.debug: module debug check failed: %d module(s) in error
gate.failed.test: module test check failed: %d module(s) in error
gate.failed.audit: module audit check failed: %d error(s) found
gate.failed.fix: Fix the reported modules, or run 'liora %s' for details.
gate.cancelled: module checks interrupted by the developer (Ctrl+C)
marketplace.flag.category: store category filter (ADMINISTRATION, COMMERCIAL, FINANCE, OPERATIONS, COMMUNICATION, DATA, AUTOMATION, SYSTEM)
marketplace.search.none.fix: Try fewer or different keywords, or browse another category.
marketplace.error.search.fix: Check the LIORIAN_STORE_API URL and your connection.
marketplace.error.download.fix: Check your connection and that the store artifact is available.
marketplace.install.already.fix: Run 'liora marketplace install %s --force' to replace it.
marketplace.install.confirm: Module %q is already installed, replace it?
marketplace.install.not_found.fix: Check the module slug/domain, or search the catalog with 'liora marketplace search'.
marketplace.error.checksum.fix: The archive was corrupted during download — retry the installation.
marketplace.error.signature.fix: The publisher signature could not be verified — do not install the module.
marketplace.error.signature.no_key: signature present but no usable public key to verify it
marketplace.error.signature.no_key.fix: Ask the publisher for a valid signature public key, or contact the store.
marketplace.error.invalid: module %q failed validation after extraction: %d error(s)
marketplace.error.manifest: the archive contains no module manifest
tui.summary.title: Summary
module.error.name_length: module name must be between 3 and 64 characters
module.error.name_kebab: module name must be kebab-case (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only)
module.error.domain: module domain must be a reverse-DNS dotted form (e.g. com.organization.domain)
module.error.version: version must follow the SemVer format (e.g. 0.0.0)
module.error.icon: icon must be a PascalCase component name (e.g. PuzzleIcon)
module.error.type: type must be one of CONFIGURATION, EXTERNAL_URL, WEB_APP_REMOTE, WEB_APP_CACHED, WEB_APP_LOCAL, REMOTE_FRONTEND, SYSTEM, SERVICE, WIDGET, THEME (INTERNAL/EXTERNAL are deprecated)
module.error.category: invalid category (allowed: ADMINISTRATION, COMMERCIAL, FINANCE, OPERATIONS, COMMUNICATION, DATA, AUTOMATION, SYSTEM)
module.error.select_article: provide the article via --id in non-interactive mode
module.error.select_workflow: provide the workflow via --id in non-interactive mode
view.error.no_module: the target module is required (provide the module folder under library/modules/)
pack.error.validation: module %q has %d validation error(s), packaging aborted
pack.error.max_size: archive exceeds the maximum size of %d MB
auth.error.no_token: no session token available — run 'liora connect'

cmd.install.long: Install a local .LiorArtifactPackage archive into the workspace, without the marketplace and without api-core. The archive is audited and validated by the same fail-closed engine as the marketplace install, then installed multi-version into library/modules/<id>/<version>/ with the current version pointer.
localinstall.warning.unsigned: archive not signed (local install — the marketplace chain remains the trust authority)
localinstall.warning.no_key: no signing key available, the .sig sidecar was not verified
localinstall.warning.unverified: signature verification failed, the archive is treated as unverified

cmd.doctor.long:
Diagnoses a module's full development loop: identity, socle binding, environment wiring, library server availability and URL scheme coherence.

With --fix, repairs what is safe to repair: creates the socle .env from its sample, wires the library transport root, provisions the mkcert certificates and binds the module to the socle.

Binding goes through `artifact bind:socle`: the socle is a separate public repository, and a standalone module repository needs no vendoring of the socle tree.
doctor.flag.socle: path to the socle (default: the module's binding, then the neighbouring socle)
doctor.detail.tls_missing: HTTPS socle without an mkcert certificate
doctor.detail.library_url_missing: NEXT_PUBLIC_LIBRARY_MODULES_URL absent — the installation registry stays empty under next dev
doctor.detail.library_same_origin: library served by the socle itself
doctor.detail.module_id_missing: manifest.id absent — the module is not addressable in any library
doctor.detail.link_absent: module not bound to any socle
doctor.detail.transport_mismatch: %s on an %s socle — the browser will block the iframe (mixed content)
doctor.detail.transport_bound: dev-server URL aligned with the socle
doctor.error.not_socle.fix: Pass --socle <path>, or run from the socle repository.
doctor.error.no_socle.fix: Clone the public socle repository, then pass --socle <path>.
doctor.hint.done: Restart the socle so its NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables are re-read, then the module's dev-server.
doctor.json.failed: the module's development loop is inconsistent
create.flag.standalone: create a standalone module repository in the current directory
create.standalone.socle: The socle is a separate repository: clone https://github.com/protorians/liorian-socle next to it, then run `liora doctor --socle <path> --fix` to prepare it. The module will then be served on https://localhost:5010/m/%s.
create.error.standalone_nested: the current directory is inside the %s project — a standalone module repository cannot be nested
create.error.standalone_nested.fix: Use a dedicated directory for the module, outside any existing project.
create.error.standalone_not_empty.fix: Create an empty directory dedicated to the module, or run the command there.
create.flag.publisher: publisher organization slug — overrides the `liora connect` session slug (CI / scripted replay escape hatch)
create.warn.domain_prefix: domain %s is not canonical for this type — prefix rewritten: %s

create.prompt.type: Module type — decides the scaffolded reference mockup and the domain prefix

create.error.not_connected.fix: Connect first (`liora connect`), then run the creation again.

create.error.org_slug_missing.fix: Run `liora create module` in an interactive terminal to define your organization slug.

connect.org_slug.unavailable: developer store unreachable (%s) — the organization slug will be required when creating a module
connect.org_slug.non_interactive: organization slug missing — run `liora connect` in an interactive terminal to define it
